title: In matched Cycle 24 and 25 months, 2 GHz flux rises 13% at fixed sunspot number
abstract: We test whether the Cycle 25 emission excess can be confined to F10.7. Common-day monthly data in January 2011 to November 2013 and January 2022 to November 2024 give a 2 GHz rise of 12.99% at matched sunspot number (conditional 95% limits 8.80 to 16.80), against 10.70% for F10.7. F10.7 divided by the interpolated 2 and 3.75 GHz flux changes by only 1.37% (0.30 to 2.45). A radio-only activity model gives 1.75% (0.62 to 2.85). These results oppose an F10.7-only explanation under stable relative scales and the fitted spectral relation. At matched Mg II, sunspot number falls 19.15%, while 2 GHz and F10.7 change by about -2%. That test retains only ten Cycle 25 months. The spot deficit changes with the time model, and 3.75 GHz shows a separate deficit. Receiver calibration, limited activity overlap and few independent blocks prevent a physical cause from being identified. We provide code, aggregate estimates, a figure, exact source hashes and a retrieval script. External observations remain outside the bundle.
